items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: read the ordinary operations off stalks, construct the signed total tensor and the injective Hom model, prove flasque acyclicity from the flasque-kernel lifting theorem, and finish with the chain-Hom adjunction. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1 pp. 339-341 (injective models in $D^+$ and the basic properties of $f_!$) and Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, SS12 (Definition 12.1, Lemma 12.2, Lemma 12.3, Lemma 12.5). Step 1 (inverse and direct image). The stalk of $f^{-1}G$ at $x$ is $G_{f(x)}$ ([[lem-stalk-inverse-image-sheaf]]), so $f^*=f^{-1}$ is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms; the inverse/direct-image adjunction ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]) is $k$-linear, and for injective $I$ on $X$ the functor $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(-,f_*I)$ is naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*(-),I)$, so $f_*I$ is injective and the chain-Hom adjunction gives $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ on $D^+$. Step 2 (tensor). Define $F\otimes_kG$ by sheafifying the sectionwise tensor presheaf; its stalks are $F_x\otimes_kG_x$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) because filtered colimits commute with finite tensor expressions. All $k$-vector spaces are flat, so tensoring is stalk-exact, and a bounded complex is K-flat: filter the finite-column total tensor against an acyclic complex by $A$-degree and use that each column is acyclic. Hence the signed total tensor of bounded representatives computes $A\otimes^L_kB$ independently of the representatives. Step 3 (internal Hom). For a bounded-below injective replacement $B\to I_B$ and a bounded representative $A$, put $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ with $d(\varphi)=d_I\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi d_A$; each $\mathcal Hom(A^p,I^q)$ is injective because it is right adjoint to the exact functor $-\otimes A^p$, the total complex is bounded below and termwise injective, and replacing $A$ or $I_B$ changes it only by a quasi-isomorphism (test on the open extensions $j_U!$ and use stalk exactness). This is the actual internal derived Hom, not a sectionwise Hom of stalks. Step 4 (flasque acyclicity). An injective $k$-sheaf is flasque since $\operatorname{Hom}(j_U!k_U,I)=I(U)$ and injectivity extends sections along $j_U!k_U\to j_V!k_V$ for $U\subset V$. Embed a flasque $F$ into an injective $I$; the flasque-kernel lifting theorem ([[lem-flasque-kernel-lifts-quotient-sections]]) makes the quotient flasque with $I(U)\to Q(U)$ onto for every open $U$, so the long exact sequence gives $H^1(U,F)=0$ and $H^{n+1}(U,F)\cong H^n(U,Q)$; induction on degree proves vanishing, and for a bounded-below flasque complex the same degreewise comparison computes derived sections on each open by the ordinary section complex. Step 5 (adjunction identities). The signed chain transposition $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C\otimes A,I)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I))$ is an isomorphism (Koszul reordering), and since $I$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I)$ are K-injective and bounded $C$ is K-flat, $H^0$ yields tensor $\dashv$ $R\mathcal Hom$ on $D^b$ with bounded-below target; restriction to opens gives the internal version, and associativity, symmetry, evaluation and currying hold on pure tensors and hence on sheaves. No constructibility of the internal Hom is asserted; that is supplied later on this page by the geometric finite conical/cochain models and the derived incidence model, which are not prerequisites of this lemma.

references.title: Jean-Louis Verdier, Dualité dans la cohomologie des espaces localement compacts, Séminaire N. Bourbaki 1964–1966, exposé 300, pp. 337–349 (Novembre 1965)

The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves (chapter 20): §12 flasque sheaves, §16 cohomology on Hausdorff quasi-compact spaces, §17 the base change map, §18 proper base change in topology, §21 cohomology with support in a closed subset, §54 projection formula

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used exactly as follows: [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] derives DC from AC, which feeds the bounded-below injective replacement [[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]] and the injective model [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]; [[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]] consumes AC through Grothendieck's injective-embedding theorem; [[lem-flasque-kernel-lifts-quotient-sections]] consumes AC through Zorn's lemma. The stalk, tensor, Hom and adjunction verifications are choice-free.

items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation. No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety, bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted to be a finite compact realization.
items.strategy: For each individual quasi-projective morphism and support collection, apply the compatible stratification theorem [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], the conical-neighbourhood theorem [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]] and the finite coiled-model theorem [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]; on the resulting finite deleted-boundary models the incidence theorem [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] proves the finite local and global cochain statements, internal-Hom constructibility and field-extension comparison, and choices for different operations need not form one jointly stratified cyclic diagram. A separated finite-type variety has a finite affine open cover with affine intersections (the diagonal is closed and each two-chart intersection is a closed subscheme of a product of affine charts, iterated); each intersection is quasi-projective, so the local construction applies, and the finite Cech derived augmentation of [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] assembles the local models into global finite bounded complexes, with uniformly bounded amplitudes and coefficient-extension compatibility. Compact-support models are assembled by the ordinary open/closed support triangles and internal Hom is locally computed on the finite affine cover with uniform bounds. AC is assumed and inherited from the geometric and analytic suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and inherited from [[thm-algebraic-whitney-strata-have-controlled-local-conical-neighborhoods]], [[lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations]] (through [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]]), [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The assembly over a finite affine cover is finite.
